architecture.mechanism: Phase transition — a threshold-triggered, non-explosive restructuring of a medium's internal state (as in water turning into ice) that redistributes energy through latent-heat exchange rather than chaotic thermal runaway.
architecture.intervention: Redesign the cooling loop as a two-phase (liquid–vapor) system: pressurize the coolant so it operates just below its boiling point, letting nucleate boiling's latent-heat absorption clamp block temperature during transients, and add a critical-heat-flux threshold sensor that vents coolant or derates the engine the instant boiling departs from the nucleate regime, preventing the insulating vapor film that precedes overheating and block rupture.
architecture.expected_effect: Cylinder-block temperature is held at the phase-change temperature even under coolant-loss transients, so heat is absorbed as latent heat of vaporization instead of raising metal temperature, maintaining cooling integrity and preventing rupture.
architecture.falsification_test: On an instrumented engine dynamometer with thermocouples embedded in the block and pressure transducers in the coolant jacket, induce a controlled coolant leak at rated load; if block temperature exceeds the material yield threshold (e.g., >150 °C) or coolant pressure exceeds the relief limit before the derate engages, the phase-transition cooling hypothesis is falsified.
